content.text: Text confirmed verbatim. I'll re-submit with the quote tightened to the operative customer-right language and the rationale stating explicitly where the Customer convenience termination right lives, so the presence of that right is unambiguous on the face of the finding.

input.quote: Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement
input.rationale: CUSTOMER CONVENIENCE TERMINATION IS PRESENT. It is granted by Section 14 (p0079): "Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement." Client may therefore terminate this Agreement at will, on written notice alone: the right is unconditional, requires no cause, default, breach or TrueLink consent, and is subject to no early-termination fee, penalty, liquidated damages or other exit charge anywhere in the document. The only consequence of Client's notice is that services run to the last day of the following month, i.e. an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, which sits inside the preferred 30-day position and comfortably inside the 60-90 day fallback. The right is drafted obliquely (as TrueLink's continuing service obligation up to Client's elected termination date rather than as an express "Client may terminate for convenience" grant), but it is substantively a customer convenience termination right and needs no redline. VENDOR HAS NO MID-TERM CONVENIENCE EXIT. Section 13 (p0078) fixes a one-year term with automatic one-year renewals. TrueLink's only unilateral cut-off is the automatic termination of Sections 2 and 3, which is cause-based (Client act/omission causing a TrueLink breach under a System or Credit Repository Agreement, or Client breach of Sections 8a-8c). The walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on under 90 days' notice) therefore does not arise mid-term, and the 12-month term also defeats the "no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term" walk-away. MINOR SHORTFALLS, NOTED NOT REDLINED. There is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is largely moot because Section 5a (p0045) invoices Hosting and Support Services monthly with payment 15 days after receipt, so fees are billed in arrears and little or nothing is prepaid. The end-of-term non-renewal notice in Section 13 is 30 days rather than 90; that right is mutual, operates only at natural expiry rather than as a mid-term exit, and shortening TrueLink's side would equally cut back our own flexibility, so flagging it would work against our party. OPEN ITEM: Section 14 opens "Subject to Section 4 hereof" and Section 4 is not in the reviewed text; the cross-references in Section 6 (p0047) indicate Section 4 concerns minimum monthly fees rather than any limit on termination, but this should be confirmed on receipt of the full Section 4 and would only be revisited if Section 4 conditions Client's right.
